newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Analysts trim NAB forecasts after weak Q3.
newsitem.headline: Analysts trim NAB forecasts after weak Q3.

text.p: Australian banking analysts on Thursday trimmed their annual profit forecasts for National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) after it posted a weak third quarter.
Analysts told Reuters they were looking to cut full-year forecasts by up to A$100 million for the year ending September.
Earlier, NAB reported a net profit of A$504 million for the three months ended June 30, well below analysts' previous forecasts of between A$530 million and A$560 million.
Previous forecasts of NAB's full-year earnings had ranged from A$2.22 billion to A$2.29 billion.
NAB nine-month earnings of A$1.643 billion were 9.3 percent higher than a year ago, but the bank's quarterly accounts show a decline in profits.
Continued pressure on interest margins in Australia was largely to blame for the weaker third quarter result.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Mike Pulman said he had now lowered his full year forecast to A$2.157 billion from A$2.25 billion.
"I think the last quarter will be marginally better (than the third quarter). Margins should continue to be squeezed and the bad debt provision may be up slightly," Pulman said.
Pulman said he was not aware of anything the bank could do to significantly improve its earnings in the last quarter.
The bank's international operations are likely to continue to record earnings growth, but the Australian businesses are declining, analysts said.
"A worrying sign is that their non-interest expenses appear to be trending higher," a Sydney-based analyst said.
NAB said its non-interest expenses rose by six percent over the same quarter a year ago, but its cost-to-income ratio of 54.8 percent was better than the June 1996 ratio of 55.3 percent.
Linda Lyon, bank analyst at BNP Equities, said she also would scale back her full-year forecast.

"I was forecasting a full year result of about A$2.28 billion and I understand the (analyst) range is between A$2.24 billion to A$2.29 billion, which would mean NAB has to make about A$630 million in the last quarter," Lyon said.
She doubted the bank could do this.

Lyon said the weak result for NAB meant Australia's other major banks, particularly Westpac Banking Corp and Commonwealth Bank of Australia, were also likely to be experiencing poor growth from domestic operations.
Bank analyst Graham Maloney, of Macquarie Equities Ltd, said he would also be adjusting down his full year forecast.
Maloney said the rise in the bank's bad debt provisions to A$122 million in the June quarter from A$66 million in the March quarter was sharper than expected by the market.
NAB blamed the rise on higher overdraft provisioning in Australia and higher general provisioning due to an increase in the group's risk-weighted assets.
NAB shares closed 45 cents weaker at A$19.05.
-- Melbourne Bureau 61-3 9286-1435
